timeline.message:
Add readiness check client

This PR introduces a new command line tool that exits with return
code 0 if Elasticsearch is up and ready to serve requests, otherwise
it exits with return code 1.
timeline.author: Nikola Grcevski

diff.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,6 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+ES_MAIN_CLASS=org.elasticsearch.readiness.ReadinessCheckCli \
+  ES_ADDITIONAL_CLASSPATH_DIRECTORIES=lib/tools/readiness-check-cli \
+  "`dirname "$0"`"/elasticsearch-cli \
+  "$@"

@@ -0,0 +1,15 @@
+@echo off
+
+setlocal enabledelayedexpansion
+setlocal enableextensions
+
+set ES_MAIN_CLASS=org.elasticsearch.readiness.ReadinessCheckCli
+set ES_ADDITIONAL_CLASSPATH_DIRECTORIES=lib/tools/readiness-check-cli
+call "%~dp0elasticsearch-cli.bat" ^
+  %%* ^
+  || goto exit
+
+endlocal
+endlocal
+:exit
+exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%

+[[release-notes-8.0.0]]
+== {es} version 8.0.0
+
+coming::[8.0.0]
+
+The following list are changes in 8.0.0 as compared to 7.17.0, and combines
+release notes from the 8.0.0-alpha1, -alpha2, -beta1, -rc1 and -rc2 releases.
+
+Also see <<breaking-changes-8.0,Breaking changes in 8.0>>.
+
+[[known-issues-8.0.0]]
+[float]
+=== Known issues
+
+* If you installed {es} from an archive on an aarch64 platform like Linux ARM or macOS M1, the
+`elastic` user password and {kib} enrollment token are not generated
+automatically when starting your node for the first time.
++
+--
+After the node starts, generate the `elastic` password with the
+<<reset-password,`bin/elasticsearch-reset-password`>> tool:
+
+[source,bash]
+----
+bin/elasticsearch-reset-password -u elastic
+----
+
+Then, create an enrollment token for {kib} with the
+<<create-enrollment-token,`bin/elasticsearch-create-enrollment-token`>> tool:
+
+[source,bash]
+----
+bin/elasticsearch-create-enrollment-token -s kibana
+----
+--
+
+
+[[breaking-8.0.0]]
+[float]
+=== Breaking changes
+
+Aggregations::
+* Percentiles aggregation: disallow specifying same percentile values twice {es-pull}52257[#52257] (issue: {es-issue}51871[#51871])
+* Remove adjacency matrix setting {es-pull}46327[#46327] (issues: {es-issue}46257[#46257], {es-issue}46324[#46324])
+* Remove `MovingAverage` pipeline aggregation {es-pull}39328[#39328]
+* Remove deprecated `_time` and `_term` sort orders {es-pull}39450[#39450]
+* Remove deprecated date histo interval {es-pull}75000[#75000]
+
+Allocation::
+* Require single data nodes to respect disk watermarks {es-pull}73737[#73737] (issues: {es-issue}55805[#55805], {es-issue}73733[#73733])
+* Remove `include_relocations` setting {es-pull}47717[#47717] (issues: {es-issue}46079[#46079], {es-issue}47443[#47443])
+
+Analysis::
+* Cleanup versioned deprecations in analysis {es-pull}41560[#41560] (issue: {es-issue}41164[#41164])
+* Remove preconfigured `delimited_payload_filter` {es-pull}43686[#43686] (issues: {es-issue}41560[#41560], {es-issue}43684[#43684])
+
+Authentication::
+* Always add file and native realms unless explicitly disabled {es-pull}69096[#69096] (issue: {es-issue}50892[#50892])
+* Do not set a NameID format in Policy by default {es-pull}44090[#44090] (issue: {es-issue}40353[#40353])
+* Make order setting mandatory for Realm config {es-pull}51195[#51195] (issue: {es-issue}37614[#37614])
+
+CCR::
+* Avoid auto following leader system indices in CCR {es-pull}72815[#72815] (issue: {es-issue}67686[#67686])
+
+Cluster Coordination::
+* Remove join timeout {es-pull}60873[#60873] (issue: {es-issue}60872[#60872])
+* Remove node filters for voting config exclusions {es-pull}55673[#55673] (issues: {es-issue}47990[#47990], {es-issue}50836[#50836])
+* Remove support for delaying state recovery pending master {es-pull}53845[#53845] (issue: {es-issue}51806[#51806])
+
+Distributed::

+* Remove per-type indexing stats {es-pull}47203[#47203] (issue: {es-issue}41059[#41059])
+* Remove translog retention settings {es-pull}51697[#51697] (issue: {es-issue}50775[#50775])
+

+* Remove the deprecated `local` parameter for `_cat/shards` {es-pull}64867[#64867] (issue: {es-issue}62197[#62197])
+
+Features/Features::
+* Remove deprecated `._tier` allocation filtering settings {es-pull}73074[#73074] (issue: {es-issue}72835[#72835])
+

+* Add lower bound on `poll_interval` {es-pull}39593[#39593] (issue: {es-issue}39163[#39163])
+* Make the ILM `freeze` action a no-op {es-pull}77158[#77158] (issue: {es-issue}70192[#70192])

timeline.body:
This PR introduces a new Elasticsearch command line tool that can serve as a readiness probe client. To determine if Elasticsearch is up we establish a socket connection to the HTTP port Elasticsearch serves requests. The client will only connect to the socket, it will not attempt to establish any communication, essentially it checks if the port is open and ready.

With this implementation we achieve the requirements for https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/81168 without any new open ports, without worrying about SSL or authentication.

Closes [#81168](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/81168)

timeline.body: Hi @grcevski, I've updated the changelog YAML for you.

I don't think this is sufficient as a readiness check. The port is opened async to when the node is ready to accept api requests (eg recoveries etc happen). This is why tests wait for green before running.

reply.body:
I consulted on this with the distributed team. My initial thought was the same, waiting for green (or yellow) before we claim we are up and running, but that would cause issues on master failover/restart, making the whole cluster appear down. Initially @DaveCTurner suggested we monitor cluster state and wait for the following condition:

```
ClusterChangedEvent.state().blocks().hasGlobalBlock(GatewayService.STATE_NOT_RECOVERED_BLOCK) == false
```

Meaning we have sufficiently recovered cluster state to claim the node is up. I believe the ports open after this happens during bootstrap.

After my initial prototype of checking for the cluster state event change, there was a high bandwidth discussion between @tbrooks8, @henningandersen and @DaveCTurner and they recommended this approach going forward.

I suppose we may need to clear-up the exact requirement, are we looking for 'green' node or just node that can respond to requests?

My earlier prototype (of just the server part) that listens on cluster change events is here: https://github.com/grcevski/elasticsearch/tree/feature/readiness_check

If a port being open is all we are looking for, then I don't see why a custom tool is needed, it seems possible to do a TCP probe in kubernetes?
https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes/#define-a-tcp-liveness-probe
Oh, I didn't know you could do TCP probes, I thought it was HTTP and call program only. Then this PR makes no sense. I'll follow-up on the issue with this resolution.

timeline.body: The cli infrastructure all seems fine, but I think there is a problem with using a simple port connection as a readiness check.
